item.title: Self-Hosted MUD Game Engines: Evennia vs RanvierMUD vs CoffeeMUD Comprehensive Guide
item.description:
Introduction

Multi-User Dungeons (MUDs) represent one of the earliest forms of online multiplayer gaming, dating back to the late 1970s. Despite the rise of graphical MMORPGs, text-based MUDs continue to thrive as a niche gaming community, valued for their deep storytelling, rich world-building, and accessibility. Modern MUD engines have evolved significantly, offering web-based clients, scripting languages, and sophisticated world-building tools that make running your own MUD server easier than ever.

item.title: Self-Hosted Chess Platforms & Engines: Lichess vs PyChess vs Fairy-Stockfish
item.description:
Introduction

Chess is experiencing a renaissance. From pandemic-era streaming to chess engine breakthroughs, the ancient game has never been more popular — and open source software has been at the center of it all. The world’s most popular chess platform, Lichess, is 100% open source and serves millions of games daily. But what many don’t realize is you can self-host your own chess server, analyze games with powerful engines, and even run chess variant platforms — all from your own hardware.
